question: what does the endpoint read when the retrieval stage is removed
design: all 48 element judgements over the 8 first-repeat confirmation artifacts, judged on the full artifact by the primary judge, compared with the span-based verdict on the same items
not_uniformly_more_permissive: four verdicts moved from satisfied to negative, so removing retrieval is not simply a looser rule; it changes the reading in both directions

comparison_with_the_detectable_effect.reading: changing the scoring method moves the endpoint by about 2.3 times the smallest effect the design was sized to detect. An instrument choice of this size is not a detail of the analysis; it dominates the comparison it is meant to serve.

why_condition_means_are_not_reported: two artifacts per condition cannot separate a condition from a task, and reporting per-condition coverage here would invite a treatment reading that the design cannot support. The aggregate shift is a property of the instrument, not of any condition.
admissibility_unchanged: these verdicts remain inadmissible for scoring, because no human-anchored calibration set exists. The figures describe what the instrument reads, not what an episode scored.
